evidence.claim: Stride describes itself as serving learners in primary, secondary, and postsecondary settings, providing K-12 education, career learning, professional skills training, and talent development, and reaching all 50 states and more than 100 countries.
Stride's annual-report evidence describes online/blended schools, Career Learning schools or programs in 27 states and D.C., and cites a large U.S. market for full-time virtual and blended schools.

Kelly Education says it helps more than 10,000 schools and more than 1,000 school districts address recruiting, hiring, and workforce management needs, including substitute teachers, school nurses, paraeducators, tutors, and K-12 support roles.
evidence.source_title: Kelly Education | K-12 Education Staffing & Workforce Solutions

evidence.claim: Kelly Education states that it supports districts through SLP, OT, PT, and mental health services and helps fill substitute teachers, special-education teams, tutors, and remote-work transitions.
evidence.source_title: About Us | Kelly Education Staffing & Workforce Solutions

evidence.claim: Scholastic's FY2025 disclosure says its Education Solutions segment includes sales to schools and libraries of children's books, print and online reference materials, classroom magazines, classroom materials for literacy instruction, and professional development covering pre-K to grade 12 in the U.S.
Scholastic reported approximately 11.3 million U.S. classroom magazine circulation in fiscal 2025, with most circulation in pre-K to grade 6.

Nerdy reported that Varsity Tutors for Schools executed 91 contracts in Q4 2024, generated $4.6 million of bookings, and enabled access for 5.0 million students at more than 1,100 school districts as of December 31, 2024.
Nerdy describes Varsity Tutors as a live online learning platform using technology and AI to deliver personalized live learning at scale.
Pearson's Connections Academy evidence says that in the 2021-22 school year, 47 Connections Academy schools in 29 states served more than 100,000 K-12 students.
Pearson Virtual Schools says it supports full-time virtual schools through Connections Academy, Pearson Online Academy, and Pearson Online Classroom.
evidence.source_title: Pearson Virtual Schools | Online Learning Solutions for K-12

memory_update.text: Stride (LRN) is the reference public operator for the K-12 virtual-school node, but should be used mainly as a benchmark to identify less obvious staffing, curriculum, tutoring, and compliance suppliers.

Kelly Services (KELYA) is a small-cap underfollowed education staffing angle tied to teacher shortages, substitute coverage, paraeducators, special education, school nurses, and district workforce outsourcing.

Scholastic (SCHL) is a small-cap curriculum/content supplier candidate; verify whether its digital and district-purchased products are used materially by virtual, hybrid, or alternative K-12 programs.

Nerdy (NRDY) is a micro-cap speculative exception with verifiable Varsity Tutors for Schools district access, but survival depends on paid conversion, liquidity, funding durability, and margin evidence.

Several highly relevant K-12 virtual-school infrastructure suppliers are private or recently taken private, including PowerSchool, Frontline Education, IXL, Edmentum, and Connections Academy operating assets inside Pearson. Later layers should map private competitors to public second-order proxies.

node: K-12 virtual schooling and alternative digital schooling platforms
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the K-12 virtual schooling node found one obvious public reference leader and three less-obvious public-market exposures: teacher/staffing supply, supplemental digital curriculum, and district tutoring/intervention. The chokepoint is not only the branded virtual school operator; it also includes state-authorized school operations, online curriculum, teacher and paraprofessional staffing, special-education support, attendance/compliance workflows, and district procurement. Candidates are research leads only, not recommendations.
